newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia to build naval base in Sabah state - paper.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia to build naval base in Sabah state - paper.

text.p: Malaysia plans to build a one billion ringgit (US$400 million) naval base in the eastern state of Sabah to beef up maritime security in the area, the New Straits Times said on Wednesday.
"In terms of security, this area is prone to piracy, murder, smuggling and the influx of illegal immigrants," the newspaper quoted Defence Minister Syed Hamid Albar as saying.
Police said they believed pirates operating out of the nearby southern Philippines islands were responsible for recent attacks on coastal towns in Sabah.
The daily said work on the 144-hectare (356 acre) site at Teluk Sepanggar, about 25 km (15 miles) from Kota Kinabalu, the state capital, is expected to start soon.
The Royal Malaysian Navy will relocate its east Malaysian naval base on Labuan island to the new site, Syed Hamid said.
